gap_notes: CyberArk vault holds Windows/AD privileged accounts but Unix/Linux and network-device passwords are onboarded inconsistently and several batch service accounts are still rotated by hand.
Privileged sessions to in-scope servers route through the PAM proxy with credential injection and direct admin paths are blocked at the network layer.
Sessions are recorded with searchable command metadata and retained per policy; high-risk command flagging is enabled though review SLAs are still being tuned.
Most privileged roles still carry always-on standing membership; JIT elevation is piloted only for a handful of cloud admin groups, so zero-standing-privilege coverage is minimal.
Scheduled discovery runs across AD and the major Unix estate but cloud, DB and SaaS local-admin accounts are scanned ad hoc and newly found accounts are onboarded manually.
Application-to-application credentials are still largely hard-coded in config and CI variables; only two strategic platforms fetch credentials from the broker at runtime.
MFA is enforced at the PAM elevation point for all in-scope access, but phishing-resistant FIDO2 is rolled out to only part of the tier-0 administrator population.
Break-glass accounts are sealed, alert-on-use, require dual control at checkout and auto-rotate after use with an auto-raised incident for review.
Standing local-admin has been removed from the standard SOE fleet but a sizeable population of developer and engineering workstations still retains local-admin pending an EPM rollout.
Privileged entitlements are not yet right-sized against actual usage; no periodic least-privilege baseline review exists and excess grants accumulate over time.
Strategic vendors connect through the recorded PAM proxy with JIT grants, but a few legacy support arrangements still rely on standing VPN and shared admin credentials.
There is no continuous cloud entitlement analysis across AWS/Azure/GCP; over-permissioned cloud identities are only found during periodic manual reviews.
Secretless privileged workload attestation has not yet been assessed; the platform team has flagged it for a future spike alongside the workload-identity program.
Privileged accounts are recertified annually as part of the broader access review, but the cadence is not risk-tiered and a meaningful share of items are bulk-approved.
Privileged session and credential-use telemetry is forwarded to the SIEM but no behavioural analytics or anomaly detection is applied to it today.
The SOC has detections for pass-the-hash and Kerberoasting via the EDR/SIEM, but DCSync and token-theft coverage against privileged accounts is incomplete and not fully correlated.
The PAM platform meets its availability and recovery targets with tested break-glass paths; cross-region failover is exercised though the full DR drill cadence is still being formalised.
